clue.text: Composer with endless determination, for example

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final letter, so the word for determination is cut short

parts.note: grit is dogged determination
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A composer is praised for his determination, as one illustration among several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it introduces Grieg as an instance, but it supplies the two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg was the Norwegian composer of the Peer Gynt music, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Type of blow cutting top of gum first

indicators.note: first says this letter is placed at the front of the other piece
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of gum
lancing is cutting open, as a surgeon lances a boil

explanation.surface: A dentist describes cutting into the top of a gum.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing blow strikes at an angle and slides off rather than landing squarely.

clue.text: Figure showing rustiness maybe in long-distance triathlon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statue or figure made of a metal that rusts
second meaning: the gruelling endurance race of swimming, cycling and running

explanation.surface: An athlete looks rusty during a long triathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: Rust is the clue that the figure is made of the metal; the race is the famous endurance event.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironman is the brand of long-distance triathlon, and a sculpture of a man in that rusting metal is a figure of the same name.

clue.text: Discovered lout visiting sadly plagued Eastern Caribbean islands

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so these letters go within the others
sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: lout without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A yob is found out while visiting some troubled Caribbean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found out, but it means uncovered: lout loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Guadeloupe is a French overseas region in the eastern Caribbean made up of several islands.

clue.text: Going after drink European departs frustrated

indicators.note: one thing going after another follows it, so the later pieces are placed behind the drink

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
E is the abbreviation for European
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A European walks off in frustration after having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: D for 'departs' is the abbreviation on railway and airline timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to thwart or put an end to it, so a scotched scheme has been frustrated.

clue.text: Recalling male shopkeeper perhaps getting dog briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the dog is dropped

parts.note: a counterman is a man who serves behind a shop counter
the dingo is the Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a male shopkeeper who owned a dog for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' looks like remembering, but here it means cancelling an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Countermanding an order revokes it, just as a company recalls a product or an official recalls an instruction.

clue.text: Current Spanish accent student dropped

indicators.note: dropped means let fall away, so the letter for the student is removed

parts.note: the tilde is the wavy accent over the Spanish ñ
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A student gives up trying to put on a current Spanish accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective for the accent, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is a current of water, the flow of the sea in and out.

clue.text: Musician playing his part

indicators.note: playing about with something means fiddling with it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician in an orchestra performs his section of the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpist plays the harp, so is a musician.

clue.text: Empty dredger, old ship delivering refuse

indicators.note: an empty word has had its insides taken out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of dredger
O is the abbreviation for old
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An empty dredger and an old ship are carrying rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun meaning rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter, rubbish or scum from molten metal, so refuse in the sense of junk.

clue.text: Defences protecting island in fact I sort of designed

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding to keep safe, so the rearranged letters wrap round the island
something designed is drawn up anew, so these letters are arranged into a fresh pattern

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone half-admits to having planned an island's defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact I sort of' reads as a hesitant admission, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortifications are walls, ramparts and other works built to defend a place.

clue.text: Fruit in volume American online supermarket stocks

indicators.note: a shop that stocks something holds it inside, so the supermarket letters hold the volume letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
V is the abbreviation for volume
Ocado is a British online-only grocery retailer

explanation.surface: A US online grocer stocks fruit in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: A and OCADO together hold V between them. Ocado is a British internet supermarket, not an American one: American only supplies the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, eaten as a savoury food.

clue.text: Experience atmosphere finally in excited ground

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other before they are rearranged
excited letters are agitated and stirred up out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone feels the atmosphere at a stadium full of excited fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited ground' paints a football crowd, but ground is just the letters to be mixed with the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or experience it, typically something unpleasant.

clue.text: Worried by criticism, what many old sports stars now do?

definitions.text: what many old sports stars now do

parts.note: a comment can be a critical remark
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Retired sportsmen fret over criticism of what they now do for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried by criticism' reads as one idea, but 'by' simply sets the two pieces side by side; 'ate' meaning worried is as in 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Many retired players become broadcasters, giving a running description of matches, which is to commentate.

clue.text: Where one might find archaeologists accommodation

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where archaeologists find somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is informal British for a rented room or lodgings, often a student's.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeologists work at excavation sites, and lodgings in British slang are also called by the same plural word.

clue.text: Forefront of controversy possibly when dismissing brand

parts.note: firing someone is dismissing them from a job
a line is a brand or range of goods

explanation.surface: Sacking a brand ambassador could put a company at the centre of controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as a figurative use: the literal sense is the front line of troops in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the firing line is to be exposed to attack or criticism, hence at the forefront of a controversy.

clue.text: Rebels scorn most info broadcast, claiming election's close

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the jumbled letters take in the extra letter
broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of election

explanation.surface: Dissenters dismiss most of the news coverage on election night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the election-coverage picture, but it signals that the letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonconformists refuse to follow established customs or the established church, so they are rebels against convention.

clue.text: Criminal type almost has my pity

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is lost
criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: type without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says a criminal sort almost has their pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy is the feeling of pity or sorrow for another's misfortune.

clue.text: Admire talent and decency

parts.note: to respect someone is to admire them
ability is talent or skill

explanation.surface: A list of three qualities one might admire in someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectability is the quality of being proper and socially acceptable, which is close to decency.

clue.text: Passage from right that enters bar

indicators.note: something that enters goes in, so this letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A passage from a text about a right of entry to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is the preposition meaning apart from.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract, a short passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Fibres regularly containing certain chemical compounds

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the chosen letters hold another word
regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of fibres
some means certain, as in 'some people say'

explanation.surface: Certain fibres are said to contain particular chemical compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The selected letters split after their first letter to wrap round the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms.

clue.text: Joint leader from start discounted

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, and it is taken away here
discounted means left out of the reckoning, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a start is a sudden shock or jolt

explanation.surface: A cut of meat, with the best part removed from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOCK loses its first letter. 'Start' looks like it means the first letter, but it is the word to be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The hock is the middle joint of an animal's hind leg, also a cut of meat from that part.

clue.text: Chaos as hot eggs served up with cold

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the eggs are written backwards

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Breakfast is chaotic as hot and cold eggs are dished out.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction or confusion, which is chaos.

clue.text: Interest shown by adult twins occasionally missing educational discussion forum

parts.note: a study is a subject one pursues with interest

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the chosen letters are removed from the other word

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters of the word are taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of twins

explanation.surface: Adult twins seem to drop in and out of view now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult' must become a synonym before the twins' alternate letters can be removed from it; the trick is that the selection comes from one word and the deletion acts on another.
explanation.definitionFit: A study group is a set of people who meet to discuss and learn a subject together.

clue.text: Advertisement charge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a poster or handbill
second meaning: an invoice or amount owed

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the cost of placing an ad, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is both a printed poster, as in 'stick no bills', and a statement of money owed.

clue.text: Echoing piece from blog, it reveres Hitchcock film

indicators.note: an echo sends a sound back, so the letters are read in the return direction
a piece from some words is a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: letters running across blog, it and reveres

explanation.surface: A blogger heaps admiring praise on a classic Hitchcock thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'blog, it rev(eres)', read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is Alfred Hitchcock's 1958 thriller starring James Stewart and Kim Novak.

clue.text: Most unsophisticated way to fall back during retreat

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway or retreat

indicators.note: falling back means moving backwards, so the word for way is read from the end

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: An army's simplest plan is just to fall back while retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like the military idea completing 'fall back', but it is a cosy hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, and the superlative gives the most unsophisticated.

clue.text: Refined young woman pursues copper, extremely touching!

indicators.note: one thing pursuing another comes behind it, so the young woman goes last

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of touching
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman chases a policeman, which is extremely moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal's symbol CU. A cut-glass accent is the clipped, upper-class British way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-glass describes a very upper-class, precise British accent, hence refined in manner.

clue.text: Composition of South Africa initially, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the letters are to be pronounced as spoken
initially points to the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the first letters of South and Africa, said as two letter names

explanation.surface: A school essay about South Africa is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials S and A, spoken as their letter names, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a short written piece on a subject, which is a composition in school terms.
